title: AI-assisted shopping is moving into mainstream product discovery and evaluation, shifting the path to purchase toward machine-mediated choice
source_unit: NielsenIQ Agentic Commerce Tracker press release and monthly Quick Question research
geography: United States, with tracker also described as covering Canada

observations.period: September 2026 publication; monthly 2026 tracker, past-month AI shopping use

denominator.unit: approximately U.S. consumers sampled monthly in NIQ Quick Question research; exact September respondent count is not disclosed

any_ai_shopping_use.unit: percent of U.S. consumers reporting use of at least one AI-powered tool to support shopping in the past month

ai_personal_shopping_assistant.unit: percent using AI-powered personal shopping assistants

mainstream_threshold.value: The release describes September 2026 as the first time reported adoption crossed 50%, after growing over the prior two quarters

observations.method: NIQ press release summarizing its proprietary monthly Agentic Commerce Tracker and Quick Question research. The source reports approximate monthly sample size and topline self-reported adoption; exact questionnaire, weighting, response rate, and September field dates are not disclosed on the page.
observations.uncertainty: The 51% estimate is a company-reported survey result with an approximate sample, not a public-use dataset or observed transaction share. Tool definitions, question wording, sampling, repeat respondents, and reporting error are not fully specified; use does not establish quality, savings, conversion, or autonomous purchasing.
observations.subgroup: U.S. consumers in NIQ's monthly 2026 Quick Question research; no public respondent-level subgroup breakdown is provided in the release.
observations.counterinterpretation: Reporting any AI shopping use may include light experimentation, comparison, or recommendation exposure rather than a purchase decision. Mainstream reported use does not mean consumers trust AI, delegate final choices, or abandon retailers and search.

denominator.unit: NIQ market and consumer-intelligence interpretation; no independent transaction denominator is reported

decision_stages.value: AI use is reported across product discovery, option comparison, value evaluation, narrowing choices, and final purchase decisions
decision_stages.unit: path-to-purchase stages named by the source

merchant_content_requirement.value: Product-content quality, digital discoverability, and structured product information are described as increasingly important to brand and retailer sales performance

measurement_shift.value: NIQ says it will measure agentic commerce as a distinct channel within its retail measurement suite

observations.method: Source-level interpretation of NIQ's reported use cases and its announced measurement response; the record keeps reported consumer use separate from firm strategy and from realized sales or conversion.
observations.uncertainty: The release is a vendor publication with commercial interests in measuring and serving agentic commerce. Its claims about tipping points, sales performance, and the shift from search-driven to AI-driven commerce are directional interpretations, not independent causal estimates.
observations.subgroup: Consumers, brands, retailers, product-content teams, digital-commerce platforms, and AI systems involved in product discovery and purchase decisions.
observations.counterinterpretation: Firms may optimize structured product information for AI systems without AI becoming the dominant source of traffic or sales. Machine-mediated discovery can coexist with human, retailer, social, and search pathways.

boundary: This record adds a current commercial-research signal on AI-assisted shopping and machine-mediated product discovery. It does not establish representative national adoption, actual purchases, savings, consumer welfare, algorithmic accuracy, retailer dependence, or causal market-share change from the NIQ release.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: NIQ publication retrieved; publication date, 51% topline, 20% recommendation use, 16% assistant use, prior-two-quarter growth claim, path-to-purchase stages, monthly approximate sample, commercial tracker description, and stated limitations cross-checked against the page.
